decisions.question: Separate shared executor contention from avoidable roster row visits
decisions.chosen: Separate shared executor contention from avoidable roster row visits
decisions.reasoning: Live analytics show old fanout and replay queries averaging seconds; cloud #105 holds their bounded replacements. Add a partial roster index and row-visit regression without claiming recovery or bypassing the rollout capacity gate.

narrative: This short (8-minute) lead session investigated roster read row-visit costs and contention from shared executor queries. The agent measured production traffic showing the old fanout and replay queries averaging in the seconds, then landed a targeted mitigation: a new partial index migration at `packages/engine/src/db/migrations/0051_agent_roster_index.sql`, a row-visit regression harness in `packages/engine/src/__tests__/conformance/agentRoster.test.ts` (dropping visits from 11,018 to 1,016), and supporting edits to `packages/engine/src/db/schema.ts`, `packages/engine/src/engine/agent.ts`, and the compact migration tests. Critically, the fix was scoped narrowly — it does not claim to resolve executor contention or bypass the rollout capacity gate. The bounded replacements for the slow fanout/replay queries live in cloud PR #105, and that dependency is explicitly recorded rather than duplicated locally. API surface and TTL semantics were preserved. Roster + migration test suites (48 tests) plus typecheck and lint all pass. Artifacts captured under `.agentworkforce/roster-0908/` and `docs/agent-roster-latency-389.{md,json}` document the latency analysis. No commits were made in this session; changes remain in the working tree on branch `fix/agent-roster-read-cost`.

decisions.question: How to address roster read cost without overreaching into shared executor contention?
decisions.chosen: Separate the two problems: land a partial roster index + row-visit regression locally; defer bounded fanout/replay query replacements to cloud PR #105
decisions.reasoning: Production measurements showed old fanout and replay queries averaging in the seconds — a symptom of shared executor contention that already has a bounded fix in flight in cloud #105. Duplicating that work locally would bypass the rollout capacity gate and conflate two independent problems.
decisions.impact: Keeps this PR narrowly scoped to an index + regression test (row visits 11,018 → 1,016), preserves API/TTL semantics, and defers to the existing rollout process for the contention fix.

conventions.pattern: Add a row-visit regression test alongside any index-based read-cost fix
conventions.rationale: Row-visit counts are a stable, migration-independent signal that a partial index is actually being used; asserting the count (e.g. 11,018 → 1,016) prevents silent regression if the planner or schema drifts.

conventions.pattern: Record cross-repo rollout dependencies in the PR/analysis notes rather than reimplementing the fix locally
conventions.rationale: Bypassing the rollout capacity gate to duplicate a cloud-side fix risks divergence and skips the gating process. Explicit dependency notes keep scopes clean.
conventions.scope: Engine PRs that touch queries also being reworked in the cloud repo (e.g. cloud #105)

conventions.pattern: Preserve API surface and TTL semantics when landing performance-only changes
conventions.rationale: Index/migration work should be transparent to callers and cache behavior so it can ship independently of feature changes.

lessons.lesson: Distinguish shared-executor contention from avoidable per-query row visits before proposing a fix
lessons.context: Live analytics attributed multi-second latencies to old fanout/replay queries — a systemic contention issue — while the roster read had a separate, index-shaped problem.
lessons.recommendation: Measure production first, then split the mitigation: fix what you own locally (index + regression) and defer systemic fixes to the owning PR/gate.

lessons.lesson: Report scope honestly — do not claim recovery of latencies you did not fix
lessons.context: The session explicitly refused to claim the index resolved executor contention, since cloud #105 is the actual fix for the slow fanout/replay queries.
lessons.recommendation: PR descriptions and retrospectives should name exactly which metric moved (row visits) and which did not (end-to-end contention latency).
